# Posit Community Support Application Draft: 4R/um

- **Organization / Initiative**: 4R/um (Statistics Denmark)
- **Application Link**: [Google Form](https://drive.google.com/file/d/18Vud7r8GTFsLolLNEu3RfjsVR4lHmbiH/view)
- **Target Budget**: ~$2,000 USD (to fund 4–5 guest speakers per year @ ~$400–$500 per speaker)
- **Key Deadlines**: Rolling applications; periodic reviews throughout the year (e.g., early January cutoff for winter cycle decisions).

---

## Overview & Submission Guidelines

Posit evaluates community support applications based on:
1. **Mission Alignment**: Advancing reproducible, open-source data science (R, Python, Quarto).
2. **Community Impact**: Clear benefit to local practitioners, researchers, or data scientists.
3. **Open Sharing**: Commitment to publishing code, slide decks, and learning materials publicly.

### Form Branching Logic
In **Question 5**, selecting **"Recurring meetup series"** skips Questions 6–15 (which pertain to annual/one-off conferences) and routes directly to **Question 16**. The responses below follow this flow, with Q6–Q15 provided in an appendix section if needed.

### Page 5 & 6: Initiative Details (Recurring Meetup Series)

#### 16. Initiative name *
```text
4R/um (R Forum, a Monthly R Exchange & Discussion Club at Statistics Denmark)
```

#### 17. Brief initiative summary *
```text
4R/um is the monthly R exchange meeting and technical discussion club at Statistics Denmark (Danmarks Statistik / DST), organized by the Data Science Lab. The name read as "forum" and plays with the four R's: Relevance, Reskilling, Reproducibility, and Research.

4R/um provides an open, collaborative forum to help civil servants, methodologists, and data analysts transition from legacy proprietary software (SAS) toward modern, reproducible open-source tools. Our monthly sessions cover practical workflows, high-performance computing, technical publishing with Quarto, package development, and database engineering.

In addition to internal knowledge sharing, we regularly host open sessions and joint meetings with the broader developer community (such as the CopenhagenR useR Group) and feature guest lectures from leading open-source package authors.
```

```text
https://ikashnitsky.github.io/4Rum/
(GitHub repository: https://github.com/ikashnitsky/4Rum)
```


#### 20. Current number of members (if applicable)


#### 21. Average attendance per meeting (if applicable)


#### 22. Frequency of meetings (if applicable)

```text
Monthly (held on the 4th Friday of each month, ~10 meetings per year).
```

#### 24. Monetary support request *
```text
$2,000 USD (Acceptable range: $1,500 – $2,000 USD)

Budget Breakdown & Justification:
• Speaker Honoraria / Travel Contributions: ~$400 USD per guest speaker (5 speakers × $400 = $2,000 USD).

Inviting external open-source leaders and package maintainers to present at Statistics Denmark significantly accelerates the adoption of modern, reproducible open-source practices across the Danish public sector. Having modest travel/honorarium funds enables us to attract top-tier domain experts from Denmark and neighboring European hubs (or provide appropriate speaker stipends for virtual international guests).
```

### Page 10: Knowledge Sharing & Additional Information

#### 31. How is your group's knowledge shared? *
```text
We are deeply committed to open science and transparent technical communication:

• Public GitHub Repository: All open presentation materials, reproducible code examples, and curated tutorials are hosted at https://github.com/ikashnitsky/4Rum and rendered as a public Quarto website at https://ikashnitsky.github.io/4Rum/.
• Open Quarto Slides: Slide decks from guest speakers and internal tutorials (e.g., sessions on Quarto, database benchmarks, arrow/Parquet, ggsql, and SAS-to-R migration) are rendered with Quarto and shared openly under permissive licenses.
• Monthly Newsletters: Monthly digests curating advancements across the R, Quarto, and Posit ecosystems are shared with participants and archived on the public site.
• Cross-institutional Collaboration: We actively bridge public-sector practitioners with the broader community through joint sessions with the CopenhagenR useR Group and other Danish academic/industry institutions.
```

#### 32. We know a form can't capture everything. If there is anything else you'd like us to know, please share it here.
```text
Statistics Denmark is at an exciting inflection point: like many national statistical institutes across Europe, we are actively modernizing our analytical infrastructure and supporting staff in moving away from proprietary legacy software (SAS) toward an open, reproducible R and Python ecosystem.

4R/um is the grassroots engine driving this cultural transformation. It has grown into a vibrant community of nearly 90 civil servants, researchers, and data engineers. Bringing prominent guest speakers into this environment creates an enormous multiplier effect—it inspires colleagues, introduces best-in-class workflows directly from the package authors, and connects public-sector statisticians to the global open-source community. Support from Posit would directly empower us to sustain high-caliber guest sessions throughout 2027.
```
